Artifacts.Name: Preparing for a Cognitive Walkthrough
Artifacts.Description: A reading that introduces the cognitive walkthrough method, explaining what it is, how it differs from heuristic evaluation, and what evaluators must define and prepare before beginning a walkthrough session.

Artifacts.Name: The Step-by-Step Cognitive Walkthrough Procedure
Artifacts.Description: A reading that walks through the step-by-step cognitive walkthrough procedure, explaining how evaluators work through each action in a task sequence and apply a fixed set of diagnostic questions to assess usability.

Artifacts.Name: Identifying and Documenting Failure Points
Artifacts.Description: A reading that covers how to systematically recognize, categorize, and document usability failure points uncovered during a cognitive walkthrough so that findings are precise and actionable enough to inform design improvements.

Artifacts.Name: Applying the Method to Peer Prototypes
Artifacts.Description: A reading that guides learners through applying the cognitive walkthrough method to real peer-created prototypes, bridging classroom instruction and authentic UX practice by evaluating actual interface designs.

Artifacts.Name: Interpreting Results and Communicating Findings
Artifacts.Description: A reading that explains how to move beyond raw walkthrough notes by synthesizing and interpreting findings into patterns, severity assessments, and clearly communicated usability reports for design stakeholders.
